appraisal_events.evidence: "Cette importance illusoire de M. Bloch père"; "Il vivait dans le monde des à peu près, où l'on salue dans le vide, où l'on juge dans le faux"; his verdict on Bergotte -- "Ce Bergotte est devenu illisible. Ce que cet animal-là peut être embêtant" -- and the family's absurd nickname "faux duc d'Aumale."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator extensively and ironically exposes Bloch père's groundless self-importance and ignorant literary pronouncements, contrasting his real insignificance with the inflated stature his household and cousinage grant him.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Naturellement, quand il y a quelque bêtise prudhommesque à dire, on peut être sûr que vous ne la ratez pas. Vous seriez le premier à lui lécher les pieds s'il était là," cria M. Bloch... "M. Nissim Bernard blessé arrêta brusquement son récit et... resta muet jusqu'à la fin du dîner."
appraisal_events.explanation: After Nissim Bernard's habitual exaggerations (claiming a close friendship with the elder Saint-Loup, an invented senatorship) embarrass the family, Bloch père publicly and cruelly berates him in front of the servant, and the family mocks his boasting, leaving him wounded and silent for the rest of the dinner.

status_effects.explanation: His sweeping, ill-founded literary judgments and his family's absurd flattery are shown by the narrator to be baseless self-importance.
His harsh public cruelty toward the dependent, harmless uncle adds a further unflattering note of pettiness.
His habitual boastful lying (the invented senatorship, the exaggerated friendship with Marsantes) is exposed by the narrator and mocked by the family.
Publicly humiliated by Bloch's insult before the household staff, he is left wounded and reduced to silence for the remainder of the dinner.

ambiguities: The surface form 'M. Bloch' is shared between the reference sheet's 'Bloch' (son) and 'Bloch père' (father) entries; several unmarked instances in this passage, including the one who delivers the harshest insult to M. Nissim Bernard ('cria M. Bloch'), are read as the father based on the passage's established pattern, but the son also jointly participates in mocking the uncle (the mock-classical name list, the Ulysses jab), so exact attribution of every instance is not fully certain.
